comparisons.peer_topic: Municipal Bond Trusts Operations and Risk Profile
comparisons.peer_summary: The Corporation administers municipal bond trusts holding highly-rated, long-term fixed-rate bonds, financing them via floating-rate trust certificates that reprice weekly or short-term to third parties. At December 31, 2024, liquidity commitments to these unconsolidated trusts totaled $1.8 billion (compared to $1.7 billion in 2023), with bonds having a weighted-average remaining life of 11.1 years; no significant write-downs or downgrades occurred in 2024, 2023, or 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and BAC serve as liquidity providers for Municipal Bond (TOB) trusts, holding liquidity commitments against these vehicles. JPM describes its obligation as conditional and limited by specific termination events (bankruptcy, taxability, downgrade) and collateral quality. BAC similarly administers these trusts and reports specific liquidity commitments ($1.8 billion), noting that no significant downgrades occurred, implying stable conditions, but does not explicitly list the same termination event triggers in the provided text. Both disclose the nature of their exposure as liquidity support for long-term fixed-rate bonds financed by short-term floating certificates.

sentences.text: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. or J.P. Morgan Securities LLC often serves as the sole liquidity or tender option provider for the TOB trusts.

The liquidity provider's obligation to perform is conditional and is limited by certain events ("Termination Events"), which include bankruptcy or failure to pay by the municipal bond issuer or credit enhancement provider, an event of taxability on the municipal bonds or the immediate downgrade of the municipal bond to below investment grade.

In addition, the liquidity provider's exposure is typically further limited by the high credit quality of the underlying municipal bonds, the excess collateralization in the vehicle, or, in certain transactions, the reimbursement agreements with the Residual holders.
The Corporation administers municipal bond trusts that hold highly-rated, long-term, fixed-rate municipal bonds.
The trusts obtain financing by issuing floating-rate trust certificates that reprice on a weekly or other short-term basis to third-party investors.

The Corporation's liquidity commitments to unconsolidated municipal bond trusts, including those for which the Corporation was transferor, totaled $1.8 billion and $1.7 billion at December 31, 2024 and 2023.
There were no significant write-downs or downgrades of assets or issuers during 2024, 2023 and 2022.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup provides liquidity services to TOB trusts, with a potential obligation to pay shortfalls if bond sale proceeds are insufficient upon early unwinding; this risk is often mitigated by reimbursement agreements with Residual holders or third parties.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Citi serve as liquidity providers for TOB trusts and explicitly mention risk mitigation through reimbursement agreements. JPM states its exposure is limited by reimbursement agreements with Residual holders. Citi similarly describes that for customer trusts, it has executed reimbursement agreements with Residual holders to reimburse the Company for any shortfall payments made under the liquidity arrangement. Both entities face obligations to pay shortfalls if bond sale proceeds are insufficient upon early unwinding, but both mitigate this via residual holder reimbursements.

sentences.text: In addition, the liquidity provider's exposure is typically further limited by the high credit quality of the underlying municipal bonds, the excess collateralization in the vehicle, or, in certain transactions, the reimbursement agreements with the Residual holders.

If this results in a shortfall between the bond sale proceeds and the redemption price of the tendered Floaters, the Company, pursuant to the liquidity agreement, would be obligated to make a payment to the trust to satisfy that shortfall.

For certain customer TOB trusts, Citigroup has also executed a reimbursement agreement with the holder of the Residual, pursuant to which the Residual holder is obligated to reimburse the Company for any payment the Company makes under the liquidity arrangement.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm acts as a liquidity provider for municipal bond securitization SPEs and stand-alone municipal bonds, required to make payments if losses or defaults occur. The Firm often has recourse to investment grade underlying assets and make-whole provisions, and facilities for municipal tender option bond trusts are classified as derivatives.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPM and Morgan Stanley act as liquidity providers for municipal bond trusts/SPEs and have recourse mechanisms. JPM notes its exposure is limited by collateral quality and excess collateralization. Morgan Stanley states it often has recourse to the underlying assets held by the SPEs and make-whole provisions, with the recourse amount often exceeding the maximum potential payout. Both disclose that the facilities are classified as derivatives and involve obligations to pay upon specific events (losses/default for MS; termination events for JPM).

sentences.text: JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. or J.P. Morgan Securities LLC often serves as the sole liquidity or tender option provider for the TOB trusts.

In addition, the liquidity provider's exposure is typically further limited by the high credit quality of the underlying municipal bonds, the excess collateralization in the vehicle, or, in certain transactions, the reimbursement agreements with the Residual holders.
The Firm has entered into liquidity facilities with SPEs and other counterparties, whereby the Firm is required to make certain payments if losses or defaults occur.

Primarily, the Firm acts as liquidity provider to municipal bond securitization SPEs and for stand-alone municipal bonds in which the holders of beneficial interests issued by these SPEs or the holders of the individual bonds, respectively, have the right to tender their interests for purchase by the Firm on specified dates at a specified price.

The Firm often may have recourse to the underlying assets held by the SPEs in the event payments are required under such liquidity facilities, as well as make-whole or recourse provisions with the trust sponsors.
